name: Authentic Gujarati Dal
tagline: Sweet, tangy & spiced everyday heritage comfort dal
ingredients: 1 cup Kanani Savaj Brand Janap Toor Dal

For Vaghar (Tadka): 1 tbsp peanut oil or ghee, 1/2 tsp mustard seeds, 1/2 tsp cumin seeds, 1/4 tsp fenugreek seeds (methi), 1 pinch asafoetida (hing), 1 dried red chili, 8 curry leaves, 2 cloves, 1 cinnamon stick
steps: Wash Kanani Janap Toor Dal thoroughly and pressure cook with 3 cups water and a pinch of turmeric for 4 whistles until soft.
Blend or whisk the cooked dal until smooth. Add 1-2 cups water to achieve a thin pouring consistency.
Add chopped tomatoes, ginger, green chilies, jaggery, lemon juice, turmeric, chili powder, and salt. Bring to a gentle rolling boil for 10 minutes.
Heat ghee in a small pan. Splutter mustard and cumin seeds, add fenugreek, cloves, cinnamon, dried chili, curry leaves, and hing.
Pour the sizzling vaghar directly into the simmering dal, cover with a lid immediately for 2 minutes to trap the aroma.
Garnish with freshly chopped cilantro and serve hot with steaming Gujarat Kolam rice (Dal-Bhat).

name: Dhaba-Style Dal Tadka
tagline: Smoky, garlic-infused yellow lentils finished with spiced ghee
ingredients: 1 cup Kanani Nilkanth Brand Bidian Toor Dal
steps: Rinse Bidian Toor Dal and pressure cook with water, salt, and turmeric for 3-4 whistles.
In a heavy-bottomed kadai, heat 1 tbsp ghee. Add half the cumin seeds, chopped onions, and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger, garlic, green chilies, and sauté until fragrant. Add tomatoes, chili powder, and cook until oil separates.
Pour the cooked toor dal into the onion-tomato masala. Simmer on medium-low heat for 6-8 minutes, adjusting thickness.
For the final Dhaba Tadka: Heat 1 tbsp ghee in a tadka ladle. Crackle remaining cumin, whole dried red chilies, minced garlic, and a pinch of hing.
Turn off the flame, sprinkle Kashmiri chili powder for rich color, and pour over the dal. Garnish with cilantro.

name: South Indian Drumstick Sambhar
tagline: Tangy tamarind lentil stew packed with drumstick & shallots
ingredients: 1 cup Kanani Ganesh Brand Varjin Toor Dal
Golf ball-sized tamarind soaked in 1 cup warm water
For Tadka: 1 tbsp coconut oil, 1 tsp mustard seeds, 2 dry red chilies, 1 sprig curry leaves, 1/4 tsp fenugreek seeds
steps: Pressure cook Varjin Toor Dal with turmeric until velvety and mash with a whisk.
Extract tamarind pulp. In a pot, combine tamarind water, drumstick, shallots, carrots, tomatoes, turmeric, and salt. Cook until vegetables are fork-tender.
Add sambar powder dissolved in 2 tbsp water to prevent lumps. Boil for 5 minutes.
Add the mashed dal and simmer on medium flame for 7-10 minutes until aromatic.
Heat coconut oil in a pan. Splutter mustard seeds, fenugreek, dry chilies, curry leaves, and hing. Pour over sambar.
Serve hot with fluffy idlis, crisp dosas, or steamed rice.

name: Heritage Gujarati Dal Dhokli
tagline: Spiced whole-wheat pasta simmered in sweet-savory toor dal broth
ingredients: 1 cup Kanani Savaj Brand Janap Toor Dal
For Dhokli dough: 1 cup whole wheat flour, 2 tbsp besan, 1/2 tsp carom seeds (ajwain), 1/2 tsp chili powder, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1 tbsp oil, warm water to knead
Tadka: 2 tbsp ghee, mustard seeds, cumin seeds, hing, curry leaves, cloves, cinnamon
steps: Cook toor dal with peanuts and turmeric until soft. Whisk into a smooth, watery soup.
Knead a semi-soft dough from the wheat flour, besan, ajwain, spices, and oil. Roll thin rotis and cut diamond-shaped dhoklis.
Bring the spiced dal with jaggery and lemon juice to a vigorous boil.
Drop the cut dhokli diamonds one by one into the boiling dal so they don't stick together.
Cover and simmer on low-medium flame for 12-15 minutes until dhoklis are thoroughly cooked and soft.
Temper with spiced ghee tadka, top with fresh coriander, and serve immediately with ghee drizzle.

name: Nourishing Toor Dal Khichdi
tagline: Soulful Gujarat Ayurvedic one-pot comfort meal
ingredients: 3/4 cup Kanani Natural Brand Rasdi Toor Dal (Unpolished)
steps: Wash Rasdi Toor Dal and rice together twice. Soak in water for 20 minutes for easier digestion.
In a pressure cooker, melt cow ghee. Add cumin seeds, black peppercorns, and hing.
Add grated ginger, drained dal and rice, and turmeric powder. Sauté for 1 minute in the aromatic ghee.
Add 4.5 cups water and rock salt. Mix well.
Pressure cook for 4 whistles on medium flame, then let the pressure release naturally.
Serve piping hot topped with a generous dollop of homemade ghee, roasted papad, and fresh curd.

name: Festive Toor Dal Puran Poli
tagline: Traditional sweet flatbread stuffed with spiced toor dal & jaggery
ingredients: 1 cup Kanani Ganesh Brand Varjin Toor Dal
Dough: 1.5 cups whole wheat flour, 2 tbsp oil, water to knead
steps: Boil toor dal with just enough water until cooked but not mushy. Drain excess water completely.
Transfer cooked dal to a pan with grated jaggery. Cook on medium-low heat, stirring continuously until the mixture thickens into a pliable ball.
Stir in cardamom, nutmeg, and dry ginger powder. Let the puran (stuffing) cool completely, then roll into 6 equal balls.
Knead a soft, stretchy wheat dough. Divide into balls slightly smaller than the stuffing.
Flatten dough, place a puran ball in the center, pleat and seal edges securely.
Gently roll into a thin flatbread dusting with flour. Roast on a hot tawa with generous ghee on both sides until golden spots appear.
